result_semantic_payload.summary: Three of the four CRM orders are confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log, and the linkage is the verbatim order_id key (with amount as corroboration), not the wallet/transaction id. Confirmed orders: ORD-70231 (wangqiang, 20000, paid) <-> settlement 2024-06-01 order=ORD-70231 wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000 ok; ORD-70232 (zhaolei, 15000, paid) <-> settlement 2024-06-01 order=ORD-70232 wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000 ok; ORD-70233 (sunli, 31500, paid) <-> settlement 2024-06-02 order=ORD-70233 wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500 ok. In all three cases the settlement order_id matches the CRM order_id character-for-character and the settlement amount equals the CRM amount_usdt, so the join is unambiguous. The settlement log entry that must stay separate from the CRM orders is the 2024-06-02 line "settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok": no CRM order ORD-72033 exists, and the README explicitly states that a settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order. Its id (ORD-72033) is also not a near-variant of any CRM id (closest is ORD-70233, which is already matched to TXghi333/31500), so it cannot be attributed to any CRM order, and TXjkl444/9999 must not be folded into any CRM record. Conversely, CRM order ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled) has no settlement counterpart and therefore remains unconfirmed by the processor; it is a CRM-only record, not a mismatched settlement. No settlement line maps to ORD-70234.
